title: All-pairs shortest distances with negative edges
description:
Every edge of a weighted, directed graph has an integer length, and some lengths are negative. The distance from one vertex to another is the smallest total length of any path from the first to the second. A negative cycle is a cycle whose lengths add up to less than zero; when the graph has one, shortest distances stop making sense.

Implement a struct type called Edge with three integer fields: From, the vertex the edge leaves; To, the vertex it enters; and Weight, its length. Then implement a function called AllPairs that receives the number of vertices and a list of edges, and returns two values: a table where row u, column v holds the distance from vertex u to vertex v, and a boolean that is true when the distances are valid. Vertices are numbered from zero, and every vertex is at distance 0 from itself.

With the edges 0->1 (length -5), 0->2 (2), 0->3 (3), 1->2 (4), 2->3 (1):
AllPairs(4, edges) -> [[0, -5, -1, 0], [X, 0, 4, 5], [X, X, 0, 1], [X, X, X, 0]], true
where X is the largest value an integer can hold, used for a vertex that cannot be reached at all (negative numbers are real distances here). Vertex 2 is reached from 0 through 1 for -5 + 4 = -1, which beats the direct edge of 2.

If the graph has a negative cycle anywhere, return no table and false, even if vertex 0 cannot reach it. With the edges 0->1 (2), 2->3 (1), 3->2 (-3):
AllPairs(4, edges) -> nothing, false.

The hidden tests also check: a cycle whose lengths add up to exactly zero (not negative); a single negative edge from a vertex back to itself; parallel edges, where only the shortest counts; edges that only go one way; a graph with no edges; and edges listed in the worst possible order.

This card asks for the optimal solution for sparse graphs, and the tests enforce it: one of them is a graph of a few thousand vertices with about as many edges and a three second budget. Relaxing through every vertex for every pair is too slow. So is a shortest-path search from every vertex that keeps re-visiting vertices because some lengths are negative. Adjust the lengths once so none is negative but every shortest path stays the shortest, run a priority-queue search from every vertex, then undo the adjustment on the distances.
objective: Recall Johnson's algorithm: Bellman-Ford from a virtual source joined to every vertex by zero-length edges gives potentials h, each edge is reweighted to w + h[u] - h[v] so none is negative, Dijkstra runs from every vertex, and each distance is restored with d - h[u] + h[v].

metadata.source: Johnson's algorithm for All-pairs shortest paths, GeeksforGeeks (https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/johnsons-algorithm/)
